title: Under the Weather
subtitle: Maya falls ill in the busiest week of the year.
paras: It started with a tickle in her throat on a Sunday evening. By Monday morning Maya had a dry cough, an upset stomach and a headache that made everything feel awful. She rang the surgery and managed to get an appointment for that afternoon, although leaving work early in the middle of a busy week was a real nuisance.

The doctor was kind but brisk. A nurse checked Maya's height and weight, then asked how well she was sleeping and how much exercise she did. Nothing about her physical health was worrying, the doctor said; it was almost certainly a virus rather than a disease that needed treatment. Her advice was simple: rest, drink plenty of water and stay at home.

On the way back, Maya called in at the pharmacy to buy some medicine for the fever. Standing at the counter, she suddenly felt her keys slipping through a hole in her coat pocket. She was about to lose them down a drain outside the door, but she caught them just in time.

She cancelled all her plans and spent the rest of the week on the sofa. On the eighth day after that first tickle, she finally woke up feeling like herself again, and she laughed at how completely a small virus had turned her careful plans upside down.
discuss: How did Maya deal with being ill so far from home? What do you do when you are ill and still have things you must get done?

items.clue: to push air noisily out of your throat
items.trick: OUGH sounds like OFF in this word.

items.clue: the part of the body where food goes
items.trick: It ends in CH, but the CH sounds like K.
AWE loses its E, and FULL loses an L: aw + ful.

items.clue: a fixed time to meet someone, such as a doctor
something that annoys you or causes problems
items.trick: U before I, and it ends in -ANCE.
EIGH as in EIGHT, then just T. No H at the end.
W + EIGHT: the number eight is hiding inside.

items.clue: physical activity that keeps you healthy
items.trick: EXER + CISE: the C comes first, the S comes last.
PH makes the F sound, and Y makes the I sound.

items.clue: an illness, often a serious one
items.trick: DIS + EASE: one S at the start.

items.clue: an opinion about what someone should do
items.trick: The noun has a C: good adviCe. The verb to adviSe has an S.
PH for the F sound, and it ends in -CY.

items.clue: something you take to get better when you are ill
items.trick: MED + I + CINE: an I in the middle.

items.clue: to be unable to find something
items.trick: Only one O. With two Os, LOOSE means not tight.

items.clue: decided that something would not happen
items.trick: British English doubles the L (American: canceled).
EIGHT + H: keep the T, then add H.

speaking: Talk about a time you were ill, or looked after someone who was. Use at least five of the sixteen words. For two of them, spell the word out loud, part by part: "ap – point – ment".
form_intro: You are registering at a doctor's surgery. Press 🔊 and write the missing word in each gap. Then check.
writing_q: Some people think that governments should spend more money on preventing illness than on treating it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
